segments: The seventeenth discourse.
saying: 'Is not this fortress sufficient for me and for you,
until God gives relief?'
And he remained with her until his brother died.
And in this year, there was a great scarcity in Egypt,
as the Nile did not rise as usual;
and people ate dead carcasses of animals, and even of human beings.
And then plague also followed the famine.
And an earthquake also occurred,
and destroyed many courtyards and high walls in Damascus, Homs, Hamath, Tripoli, Tyre, Acre, and Samaria;
and it reached as far as the country of the Romans {Byzantium},
though in the East it was not strong.
And in the year fifteen hundred and ninety-eight [of the Greeks],
which is 598 of the Arabs [1201/1202 AD]:
Khwarazmshah Muhammad, son of Tekish, went to the land of Khorasan,
and took from Ghiyath al-Din and from his brother Shihab al-Din the city of Merv and Nishapur,
because they belonged to him.
And when he had gone to Khwarazm and was occupied with the death of his father,
Ghiyath al-Din had taken them.
And when he sent and said to him:
'I did not expect this from you,
but that you would be a help to me against the Chinese {Kara-Khitai};
and since you did not help me,
it was not right for you to harm me.'
And when he did not return the cities to him peacefully,
he came and took them by the sword.
And Ghiyath al-Din was worsted by him,
because he was crippled by the disease of gout,
and his brother Shihab al-Din was fighting with the Indians.
And in the year fifteen hundred and ninety-nine [of the Greeks],
which is 599 of the Arabs [1202/1203 AD]:
Malik al-Adil Abu Bakr, son of Ayyub,
lord of Egypt and Damascus,
sent armies with his son Malik al-Ashraf Musa against Mardin,
and besieged it for many days,
and gained control over its villages and its territory.
Then the lord of Aleppo, Malik al-Zahir Ghazi, son of Saladin, mediated between them,
and made peace on the condition
that the lord of Mardin should give al-Adil one hundred and fifty thousand akçe dinars,
that is, white {silver} [coins],
each dinar being six zuzey {dirhams},
and should proclaim al-Adil as king,
and write his name on the dies of the dirhams and dinars.
And Malik al-Zahir took twenty thousand dinars out of that amount,
and also the village of Quradi from the district of Shabakhtan.
And al-Ashraf left and departed.
And at this time, the Turcomans were causing great destruction in the lands...
